per_claim.claim: A 1D-CNN surrogate trained on MC-generated flux spectra can predict outgoing neutron spectra with accuracy comparable to the MC ground truth for single-material shields it was trained on.
per_claim.evidence: Replication used OpenMC (not PHITS) and a reduced energy range (1-19 MeV vs 1-250 MeV); CNN predictions matched MC integral fluxes closely but dose rates diverged significantly (errors up to 850%), indicating spectrum shape mismatch.

per_claim.claim: The CNN model interpolates to unseen thicknesses and to a new material (HD concrete, rho=4 g/cm3, not in training) via density-as-material-identifier.
per_claim.evidence: Interpolation to unseen thicknesses and materials was tested; for concrete and BPE, dose errors were lower (6-24%), but for steel, errors were much higher, suggesting partial support in limited cases.

per_claim.claim: Multi-layer shielding can be handled by chaining the CNN layer-by-layer even though training used only single materials; agreement with PHITS is within about a factor of 2.
per_claim.evidence: Replication did not report results for multi-layer configurations; only single-material cases were evaluated.

per_claim.claim: Once trained, one CNN inference for outgoing flux takes ~20-30 ms on a single-core CPU; a 2500-point sweep is feasible in minutes vs several MC hours.
per_claim.evidence: CNN inference time was measured at ~104 ms per sample, and a sweep of 240 calls took ~26 s, supporting the claim of rapid evaluation compared to MC.

per_claim.claim: Training the CNN takes ~30-60 minutes on a single-core CPU once the MC training set is generated; convergence reached at ~20 epochs; loss = MAE; split 70:30.
per_claim.evidence: Training completed in ~60 s (smaller dataset), 20 epochs, MAE loss, 70:30 split, matching paper's description.

one_line: Replication partially supports claims for speed and training, but accuracy for dose rates is much lower, and multi-layer cases were not tested.
notes: Replication used open-source OpenMC instead of PHITS, and was limited to 1-19 MeV due to nuclear data constraints; spectrum shape errors led to large dose discrepancies, especially for steel. No public code/data from the original paper, so CNN was rebuilt from description. Multi-layer chaining not evaluated.
